source_documents.title: Elucidating Nonradiative Relaxation of Charge-Transfer-Type Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters: The Vibrational Effect

conditions_studied: solution: N2-saturated 1,4-dioxane, THF, DMF (steady state, fs transient absorption)

reference_evidence_units.quote: Despite comparable CT character, emitters exhibit fluorescence quantum yields differing by up to two-orders-ofmagnitude, originating from largely differed kNRS.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PXZ-TRZ, DMAC-TRZ, PXZ-DPS, DMAC-DPS
reference_evidence_units.statement: ΦF in dioxane: PXZ-TRZ 4.55%, DMAC-TRZ 41.5%, DMAC-DPS 68.2% (Table 1); the spread comes from kNRS.

reference_evidence_units.quote: By applying the Englman−Jortner energy-gap law and the Jortner−Bixon model, we quantitatively reveal the vibrational effect on kNRS: (1) kNRS of D−A and D-A-D emitters is dominated by high- (∼900 cm−1) and low-frequency (∼60 cm−1) modes, respectively;
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four
reference_evidence_units.statement: Energy-gap-law fits split kNRS into high-frequency (D-A) and low-frequency (D-A-D) promoting modes.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the more rigid DMAC donor reduces the reorganization energy, thereby suppressing the vibrational promotion of kNRS
reference_evidence_units.subject: DMAC vs PXZ emitters
reference_evidence_units.statement: The DMAC donor lowers reorganization energy and kNRS.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These results demonstrate that the emitting S1 state of all four CT-TADF molecules shares a comparable long-range CT nature, yet their ΦF values differ strikingly.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four
reference_evidence_units.statement: Large excited-state dipoles and CT ~87-91%: S1 is long-range CT in all four.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Taken together, the I→II process can be assigned to the charge-transfer evolution on S1 state, where species I corresponds to the directly populated LE state and species II to the relaxed CT state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four

reference_evidence_units.quote: Therefore, the rapid increase in kNRS with decreasing ΔES1/S0 results from the combined effects of the reduced energy gap and enhanced vibrational coupling, rather than from the energy-gap decrease alone.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four
reference_evidence_units.statement: Polarity raises kNRS through both a smaller gap and stronger vibrational coupling.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Nevertheless, DA-D emitters exhibit substantially slower kNRS than their D−A analogues (Table 2), indicating the strong electron-vibration coupling in D-A-D emitters cannot lead to efficient promotion of kNRS.
reference_evidence_units.subject: D-A-D vs D-A
reference_evidence_units.statement: D-A-D emitters decay nonradiatively more slowly.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: S1 is a long-range CT state (Lippert-Mataga dipoles, LE→CT evolution in fs-TA); shared by all four, so it does not explain the differences.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The paper's explanation of the ΦF differences is the S1/S0 nonradiative rate kNRS, analysed with the energy-gap law and vibronic coupling (Jortner-Bixon); CT character is comparable. The rigid DMAC donor lowers kNRS (ΦF 41.5% in dioxane).

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Donor rigidity and low-frequency modes enter as vibronic coupling in the energy-gap law, not as a restricted motion (boundary of guideline §3.5, first bullet, awaiting the author); not labelled RIM.

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: S1 is a long-range CT state (Lippert-Mataga dipoles, LE→CT evolution in fs-TA); shared by all four, so it does not explain the differences.

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Not discussed for this molecule in the source.

mechanism_decisions.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Not discussed for this molecule in the source.

mechanism_decisions.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The paper's explanation of the ΦF differences is the S1/S0 nonradiative rate kNRS, analysed with the energy-gap law and vibronic coupling (Jortner-Bixon); CT character is comparable. The rigid DMAC donor lowers kNRS (ΦF 41.5% in dioxane).

mechanism_decisions.label: TRIPLET_ISC_RTP_TADF
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Studied as TADF emitters, but the paper analyses only the S1/S0 decay; no delayed fluorescence or RISC measured here.
